method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05; a seat-neutral core (niis-core.l4, with eight regulative rules), date helpers (niis-dates.l4, built-in date functions, no daydate import, no YMD) and a seat layer (niis-seat.l4) that restates no rule; exported questions take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: National Injury Insurance Scheme (Queensland) Act 2016 (act-2016-034), the version in force from 2024-07-01 (current on 2026-11-06), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-2016-034.txt (unofficial HTML conversion). Not deposited and asked as facts: the National Injury Insurance Scheme (Queensland) Regulation 2016 (eligibility criteria, buy-in injuries and contribution, payment limits, the s 17(4) waiting period, prescribed exclusions); the Motor Accident Insurance Act 1994 s 39 notice day; the court rules' appeal period; the QCAT Act time for review; the value of a penalty unit; Queensland public holidays.

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run niis-dates.l4 ; l4 run niis-core.l4 ; l4 run niis-seat.l4 ; l4 run niis-cases-injured-person.l4
checks.result: 193 assertions written, 193 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-11-07, after the verification fixes); 7 #TRACEs with an expect line, each ending in the expected breach
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: From the seat of the injured person, chapter 2 (the scheme) with the review chapter and the person's offences: ss 4, 7 and schedule 1 (serious personal injury, prescribed vehicle, uninsured motor vehicle); s 9 (excluded treatment, care and support); s 10 (finalised claim); s 12 (eligibility); s 13 (buy-in); ss 16-18 (applying); ss 22(1)-(6), 23 (accepting or refusing, lifetime acceptance, refusal after a s 44(3)(a) payment without severe financial hardship, conditions); ss 21-24, 29, 31-32, 36-39 with schedule 1 (decision-making period, deemed refusal); schedule 1 participation period, ss 45(3), 46-48 (interim to lifetime); ss 35-37 with s 52(6) (payment requests); ss 40-44 (preservation notice, the agency's contribution, accepting awarded damages); ss 49-50, 52 (leaving Australia, suspension); s 53 (telling the agency of a claim); ss 105, 107, 109-110, 112, 118(3), 123, 127 (reviews and the medical tribunal); ss 50, 53, 132, 133, 134 (penalties, the s 133(2) exception, the prosecution time limit). Out: chapter 1 machinery (ss 1-3, 5, 6, 11), s 14 and s 15 (used, not asked), s 19-20 (form contents), ss 25-27 and 28-34 (assessment, support plans, service requests and funding agreements: the agency's discretion), s 51, chapters 3-5 and 7 (the agency, funding, levy, recovery, the commission, information exchange; the s 131(4) offence binds an entity given information, not the injured person), ss 113-117, 119-122, 124-126, 128-129 (tribunal procedure); s 8 and s 33 (definition and overview); s 23(1), s 38, s 47(2) (who is notified and in what form); s 54 (electronic applications); s 111 (asking for a decision notice), ss 135-149, and the regulation.
seat: the injured person (someone seriously injured in a motor accident in Queensland who applies to the scheme or participates in it, or a parent, guardian or other person acting for them)
